Among my duties as a Land Management Specialist is the reception of the areas necessary for the construction of the railway project, as well as the areas required for the relocation of public utility networks located within the old railway corridor.

This occupation phenomenon, which occurs in Colombia, is due to the abandonment of the old railway corridors. As a consequence, public utility companies—with the consent of the State and within the framework of the urban growth of the municipalities—installed their new public utility networks within these abandoned corridors.

The process of acquisition and affectation of these land areas is known in Colombia as land management, in which properties of both public and private nature may be required. For this reason, the respective owners must be compensated for such affectations, given that a portion of their property will be segregated.

General stages of the process

1. Identification and property studies

  • Information gathering for each property: full identification by real estate registration number, property nomenclature, and owner's name, assigning a consecutive code. (ANI)
  • Preparation of the "property record": with the technical and legal data of the property.
  • Title study: to verify the legal status of the property.

2. Appraisal

  • A commercial appraisal of the property is carried out and, when applicable, the procedure for updating areas and boundaries is followed in accordance with IGAC regulations (Resolution 0193 of 2014, which regulates the updating of capacity and/or boundaries according to article 26 of Law 1682 of 2013).
  • As long as the entity (or Concessionaire) complies with the legal term established to carry out the appraisal, the owner cannot demand a second appraisal within that same process.

3. Negotiation and acquisition

There are two main ways to acquire the property:

  • Voluntary alienation: the owner accepts the formal purchase offer, which is perfected by public deed and its respective registration in the real estate registration folio, thus allowing the physical delivery of the property.
  • Expropriation (in the absence of an agreement): can be processed administratively or judicially. According to the technical appendices of the ANI, this route includes stages such as the start of the administrative expropriation process, the filing of appeals, and the execution of the expropriation.

4. Delivery and compensations

  • Physical delivery of the property to the entity or concessionaire.
  • Recognition of socioeconomic compensations when appropriate: estimation of the compensation plan and recognition of social compensations per affected social unit.

Key points for owners

  • There are two decisive moments in the process: first, negotiation based on commercial prices (it is recommended to seek advice from an expert in the applicable regulations); if an agreement is not reached at this stage, an executive procedure proceeds in which the entity can acquire the asset, no longer at a commercial price, but based on the cadastral appraisal value.
  • Once the property is declared of public utility, no authority may grant construction, urbanization, or operation licenses for it. The owner may continue to inhabit it until the land management process ends or until the property is delivered.

Relevant regulatory framework

  • Law 1682 of 2013 (transport infrastructure)
  • IGAC Resolution 0193 of 2014
  • Technical guidelines of the ANI (National Infrastructure Agency) for road concession projects (4G, among others)
